clue.text: Can Noel put up inspiring names for ex-Liverpool player?

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the word takes the other piece inside it
in a down clue, putting a word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the singer Noel might reel off names to identify a former Liverpool footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns NOEL into LEON, which takes in NN to make LENNON. The player is a member of the band from Liverpool, not a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a Beatle, and the Beatles were a band from Liverpool, so he played for that city's most famous group.

clue.text: What you're after is very much current in airport

parts.note: so, as in 'so tired', means very much

indicators.note: in places the current piece within the airport

parts.note: Luton is an airport north of London
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A traveller is told the thing they want is flowing abundantly at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTON is an airport north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A solver is after the answer to a puzzle, and an answer is a synonym of the word that fits here.

clue.text: Like poker in bed, it makes you passionate

definitions.meaning: the plant kniphofia, grown in flower beds

explanation.surface: A racy line suggesting that something in bed stirs up desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not a place to sleep; the poker is a garden plant, not a card game or fire iron.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden flower is named for the glowing colour of its spikes, and the same phrase describes fiery, ardent feeling.

clue.text: Cheats in game

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to swindle or con them
female deer are hunted as game

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of cheating during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing someone out of money is swindling them; female deer are game animals in hunting.

clue.text: See 11
Baffle Tory minister left inside plant

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle or puzzle them

indicators.note: inside places the left piece within the minister's name

parts.note: Michael Gove was a Conservative cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is left confused by a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was a Conservative (Tory) cabinet minister in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is a tall flowering garden species with bell-shaped blooms, an example of the broad category named.

clue.text: Umbellifer Virginia stuck in box

indicators.note: stuck in puts the state's abbreviation within the theatre box

parts.note: a loge is a box in a theatre
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A plant from Virginia has been put in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovage is a herb in the carrot family, whose flowers grow in umbrella-shaped clusters called umbels.

clue.text: Dearest one's worth nothing in court

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment for a sweetheart
on a tennis court a zero score has its own name

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that a beloved partner counts for nothing in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is addressed with this endearment, and tennis scoring uses the same word for zero.

clue.text: Working on English broadcast alone

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
seed broadcast is scattered, or sown

explanation.surface: Someone works on an English radio programme by themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio but means scattered, as seed is.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without company is an idiomatic way of saying solo or unaccompanied.

clue.text: Section of cornice, very large, split into rings

parts.note: an O is shaped like a ring

indicators.note: very large is split, its two letters going either side of a ring

parts.note: an O is shaped like a ring
an O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A very big piece of moulding has been cut into circles.
explanation.walkthrough: V and L are separated: V goes between the first two O's and L between the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex quarter-round moulding, often forming part of a classical cornice.

clue.text: Big hash made of hugs and kisses here

definitions.text: Big hash made of hugs and kisses here

parts.words: Big hash made of hugs and kisses here
parts.note: the hash sign # is the grid of a game in which players write O's (hugs) and X's (kisses)

explanation.surface: A big mess is made of romantic hugs and kisses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hash' is not a mess but the # symbol; at the end of a letter O is a hug and X a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's game is played on a grid like a large hash symbol, filling squares with O's and X's.

clue.text: Dance about among Anglicans from same family

indicators.note: among puts the dance inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

indicators.note: about means the word for the dance is turned round

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A dance is performed among members of the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives OGNAT; Anglicans belong to the Church of England, hence its abbreviation, and 'among' reads as a container signal rather than a social setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate words or relatives share a common ancestry or origin, being related by descent.

clue.text: Live session beginning during leave

indicators.note: during places the first letter within the word for leave

parts.note: to exit is to leave

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter of session

explanation.surface: A live recording session starts while someone is on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as an adjective (a live session) but is the verb, to be alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To live is simply to be, to have being, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Journey breaks prevent lots of deliveries

parts.note: to stop something is to prevent it
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so several overs are lots of deliveries

explanation.surface: Breaks in a journey hold up a stream of parcel deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' are cricket balls bowled, not parcels; an over is a set of six of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller's brief halt partway along a route is a break in the journey.

clue.text: Spooner's enormous place is waterlogged

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: whopping means enormous
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone's huge house is flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of WHOPPING SET gives the answer by sound, with the H dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drenched through with water is completely soaked, so the phrase means saturated.

clue.text: Realise residents picked up food

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: to suss is to realise, and tenants are residents

explanation.surface: Someone works out that the residents have collected their meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment that keeps a body going is a general synonym for what we eat.

clue.text: After surgery, isn't ESP common? No, that's bonkers

indicators.note: after an operation the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether telepathy is commonplace after an operation, then dismisses the idea as crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means not of sound mind, i.e. mad or crazy.

clue.text: Rusty old team faded about halfway through Tests

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

indicators.note: about means the word for faded goes round the middle letter

parts.note: to die away is to fade, so faded is died

indicators.note: halfway through takes the letter at the middle of Tests

explanation.surface: An out-of-practice veteran side wilted midway through a cricket Test series.
explanation.walkthrough: XI (eleven) is a cricket or football team; Tests are international cricket matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust forms when iron combines with oxygen, so rusty metal has reacted with that gas.

clue.text: Cover Republican states during half term

indicators.note: during places the middle pieces within the first half of term
half takes the first two of the four letters of term

parts.note: to aver is to state

explanation.surface: A Republican makes a statement in the middle of a school or parliamentary term.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover a distance or ground is to cross it, so the verb means go across.

clue.text: Negates new uni lecturers providing ideas occasionally

parts.note: U is short for university
L stands for lecturer, doubled for the plural
if means providing, as in a condition

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of ideas

explanation.surface: Fresh university lecturers cancel things out by only sometimes offering ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the first, third and fifth letters of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to cancel it out or render it void, a direct synonym.

clue.text: She's fetching royal couple after game

indicators.note: after puts the royal letters behind the game in the answer

parts.note: loo is an old card game
K is the abbreviation for king, the first of the royal pair
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen, the second of the royal pair

explanation.surface: A woman goes to collect a king and queen after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fetching' means attractive, not collecting.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive person is informally called this, so 'she's fetching' means she is a good-looking person.

clue.text: Seeing Red, proletarian group turns

indicators.note: turns means the cluster of letters is read backwards
group points to a cluster of letters within the word proletarian

explanation.surface: A furious workers' collective changes direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' suggests communism to fit the proletarian surface, but seeing red is being angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming furious, so the phrase means very angry.

clue.text: Press starts to investigate Conservative with forked tongue?

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Reporters begin probing a Conservative politician suspected of lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists but is the verb, to iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with forked tongue means saying one thing and meaning another, as sarcasm does.

clue.text: Swinish behaviour also upended call boxes

indicators.note: boxes means the word for call encloses the other piece

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

indicators.note: upended means the word is turned the other way round

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: Piggish conduct as someone also tips over phone boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' gives OOT. 'boxes' looks like phone boxes being tipped over, but it is the verb, meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs dig in the ground with their snouts, so this activity is typical of swine.

clue.text: Angler hooks over 40 perches

indicators.note: hooks means the fishing word catches the other letter inside it

parts.note: a rod is a fisherman, by transference from the fishing rod
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A fisherman catches more than forty fish on bird perches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perches' are old units of land area, not places for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The rood is an old British measure of land area equal to forty square perches, a quarter acre.

clue.text: Mass killer caught Lahore ill-prepared

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: ill-prepared means the letters are made up badly into a new order

explanation.surface: A murderer was arrested in the Pakistani city of Lahore, which was not ready.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease has killed huge numbers of people in epidemics, so it is a killer on a large scale.

clue.text: Religious texts found in church loft

indicators.note: found in places the texts within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Holy writings are discovered in the attic of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon loft is a shelter for birds, just like a dovecote.

clue.text: Plant by drilling holes

indicators.note: drilling means the letter bores into the holes

parts.note: an O is a round hole, and an eye is a hole, as in a needle
X means by, as in 3 by 4 dimensions

explanation.surface: Something is planted by boring holes in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a common wildflower, an example of a flowering species.

clue.text: Spear-carrier's last to go home, so ends outside

indicators.note: last to go means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a spear-carrier is a walk-on actor, an extra
in means at home
sic is Latin for so, thus

explanation.surface: A minor actor's final scene goes home, so the play ends outside.
explanation.walkthrough: A spear-carrier is a bit-part actor with no lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic qualities come from outside a thing rather than being part of its nature.
